parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **economic growth**?
choices: An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP
GDP divided by the population showing the average output per person
A period of negative economic growth for two consecutive quarters (six months) or more
The level of material well-being of people in a country often measured by real GDP per capita

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of GDP per capita
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of recession
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of standard of living

A period of negative economic growth for two consecutive quarters (six months) or more

parts.text:
Last year, Zentara experienced rapid economic growth of 7.1%, while inflation rose to 6.0%.

Explain why faster economic growth might be accompanied by rising prices.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Rapid growth increases total demand (1) and if supply cannot keep up, firms raise prices (1), so demand-pull inflation rises, as shown by inflation of 6.0% when growth reached 7.1% (1)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **unemployment**?
choices: Long-term unemployment caused by a decline in an industry so workers' skills no longer match available jobs
A measure of unemployment based on the number of people claiming unemployment-related benefits
The situation where people of working age who want a job and are available for work are without paid employment
Unemployment that occurs at certain times of the year when demand for some workers falls, such as in tourism

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The situation where people of working age who want a job and are available for work are without paid employment)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of structural unemployment
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of claimant count
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of seasonal unemployment

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **unemployment rate**?
choices: The percentage of the labour force that is unemployed
Long-term unemployment caused by a decline in an industry so workers' skills no longer match available jobs
Unemployment caused by a fall in demand during a downturn or recession in the economic cycle
Short-term unemployment when people are between jobs or searching for their first job

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The percentage of the labour force that is unemployed)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of structural unemployment
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of cyclical unemployment
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of frictional unemployment

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **labour force**?
choices: Unemployment caused by a fall in demand during a downturn or recession in the economic cycle
A measure of unemployment based on the number of people claiming unemployment-related benefits
Long-term unemployment caused by a decline in an industry so workers' skills no longer match available jobs
The number of people of working age who are either in work or actively looking for work

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (The number of people of working age who are either in work or actively looking for work)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of cyclical unemployment
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of claimant count
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of structural unemployment

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **balance of payments**?
choices: The exports and imports of services such as tourism, banking and insurance
A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world
Goods and services sold to other countries
When the value of money flowing out on the current account is greater than the money flowing in, e.g. imports exceed exports

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of trade in services
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of exports
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account deficit

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **current account**?

A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world
When the value of money flowing out on the current account is greater than the money flowing in, e.g. imports exceed exports
The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account surplus
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of balance of payments
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account deficit

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **redistribution of income**?
choices: When people do not have enough income to meet basic needs such as food, shelter and clothing
The transfer of income from some groups to others usually from richer to poorer households through taxes and benefits
When people have income far below the average in their country, so they cannot afford the normal standard of living
Payments by the government to individuals such as unemployment benefit or pensions, to support incomes

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The transfer of income from some groups to others usually from richer to poorer households through taxes and benefits)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of absolute poverty
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of relative poverty
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of welfare benefits

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **absolute poverty**?
choices: A tax where the percentage of income paid rises as income rises
Payments by the government to individuals such as unemployment benefit or pensions, to support incomes
A tax where the same percentage of income is paid whatever the level of income
When people do not have enough income to meet basic needs such as food, shelter and clothing

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (When people do not have enough income to meet basic needs such as food, shelter and clothing)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of progressive tax
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of welfare benefits
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of proportional tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **fiscal policy**?
choices: Cutting government spending and/or raising taxes to reduce total demand
The total amount of money owed by the government built up from past borrowing
The use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy
A tax on spending on goods and services, such as VAT or excise duties

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of contractionary fiscal policy
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of national debt
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of indirect tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **direct tax**?

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **monetary policy**?
choices: The bank that controls a country's monetary policy and issues its currency
The rate of inflation the central bank aims to achieve such as 2% a year
The use of interest rates and the money supply by the central bank to influence the economy
When the central bank creates new money to buy financial assets and increase the money supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The use of interest rates and the money supply by the central bank to influence the economy)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of central bank
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of inflation target
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of quantitative easing

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **supply-side policies**?
choices: The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas
Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour
Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible
The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **infrastructure**?
choices: The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband
Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour
The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of supply-side policies
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **deregulation**?
choices: Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour
The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband
Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of supply-side policies
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **labour market reform**?
choices: The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition

rows.answer:

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **tax incentives**?
choices: The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband
Reductions in taxes designed to encourage firms to invest or people to work

Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **labour mobility**?
choices: The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas

Reductions in taxes designed to encourage firms to invest or people to work

parts.text: The main aim of supply-side policies is to

increase the budget deficit
increase the productive capacity of the economy
reduce exports
